body.heading: Words that point to places
paragraphs: A preposition is a word that tells us where something is. Mango is very good at showing us. Watch where he goes!
Read each line out loud, then try it yourself with a toy: put it in, on and under a box.

body.heading: In, on, under
paragraphs: The ball is in the basket.
The ball is on the table.

body.heading: Behind, in front of, next to
paragraphs: Mango is in front of the door.
The cup is next to the plate.

body.heading: Above, below, between
paragraphs: The bird is above the roof.
The fish is below the water.
The frog sits between two stones.

body.heading: Think and talk
paragraphs: 1. Hide a toy and give clues with position words: 'It is under something soft. It is next to the chair.' Can your partner find it?
2. Where is Mango right now in the picture at the top? Use two prepositions in your answer.

takeaway: Prepositions like in, on, under, behind and between tell us exactly where something is.
materials: Just you and this page — no materials needed
supervision: A grown-up nearby is recommended for younger readers; the think-and-talk questions work well read aloud together.
safetyNotes: Reading only — no physical activity or materials are involved.
screenFreeExtension: Play 'Where is it?' around the room: one person hides a toy, the other hunts using only position-word clues.
